english: Nice job stealing that key.
That Coinlord fellow was probably just gonna say some annoying stuff anyway.
Hm. There it goes.
The first day on the job.
You did GOOD.
Well.
You did well. Good is for the gods.
As you approach the bedroll you think to yourself:
Is there anything else you need to do before sleeping?
(Think about it.)
Nothing comes to mind.
But you feel it.
The youth gathering. Yelling.
Two sides, each holding an idealized view on the world, their voices echoing across the shipyard.
THE YOUNG & DUMB.
On Waterlane.
YES.
Exhaustion. It wrecks your body.
DANGER would follow... if you head out in this state.
Trouble on Waterlane View? There's always trouble there.
It's a simple teenage rebellion. They can sort it out themselves.
Hm. You should help them.
YES! I'll head down right now. Down to Pillar Crossing, past the bridge. (Leave. Right now.)
Nah. I'll skip. (Just go to sleep.)
Your gut is telling you: DIVE into this bedroll.
You should listen.
Or?
OR: You could push yourself.
Take a deep breath. Steel your body and mind.
And go deal with this ominous calling to Waterlane.
Push yourself. PUSH. YOURSELF.
Staring at your bedroll. Hands clasped. Head low.
You RISE. In spirit and flesh.
Oh. I'm not exhausted anymore.
You are not.
All it took was a push, for a good cause!
But I'm still not sure what's happening down on Waterlane, right?
Then I shall go. To Waterlane. And see what the fuss is all about. Right?
Staring at your bedroll, your weary bones begin to falter.
No amount of pushing is going to get you through this level of exhaustion.
Yeah. Probably right.
I could still try. Go see whatever's happening down on Waterlane?
The decision is yours.
The young kind.
The angsty kind.
The kind of trouble that needs WRANGLING by THE CLERIC!
Pitiable.
Understandable. You would probably only make it worse.
Before you lies a bedroll.
Your body is WORN.
You must rest. NOW.
Why do I have to sleep?
No really, what is this thing?
E-Stop staring at the bedroll.
You sit there, your body burned down to its frays.
Holding it together, just barely, after many failures.
(Groan.)
You are destroying yourself for the quest.
As many men should.
And you will never be the same...
<wiggle>...</wiggle>
No. Your body is not tired enough.
Go make some money instead, you lazy bum.
Wanting to sleep for more than 8 hours a day is a sign of mental instability. Are you okay?
Stress. Troubling thoughts. Life-threatening events.
Your body is still adjusting.
Why would you ever need to sleep? A true man works until his bones break.
Yes. Your body is weary.
It's a waste of time. But sure, go ahead.
A little nap might be good for you. And your manhood.
That's the spirit!
If you stay awake for more than 48 hours, you will die.
If you stay awake for more than 48 hours, your body will cease to function in its current state.
Which is not good for your physical health.
For now, you should not go to bed.
You should go to bed now.
Taking a long rest restores your hit points, hit dice, lowers your exhaustion to zero, and returns your spent spell slots.
A long rest lasts 8 hours, and you can take one after 20:00 each day.
Hm?
It's a... bed.
You're unsure.
It doesn't look like a bed.
Textiles. Leather-bound and filled with some soft material.
Leather-bound and filled with ox-clippings.
Most likely Bubble Yarn.
Somewhat soft.
A bed-roll.
I see. Like one of those things adventurers use when sleeping on a journey.
A real man can sleep anywhere.
Including this rugged piece of rug.
This is going to hurt your back...
At least there's no snoring here. Remember the barracks?
You hear only wind here - and the occasional giant seagull call.
It will be a good place to rest.
Staying within the confines of the Guard Tower, you successfully spend eight hours on your long rest.
No need to roll any encounters. You've had enough for one Adventuring Day. Now let's see...
Getting into the tea shop on day one? That's impressive.
Just remember to investigate it properly before reporting back to the goblins.
Getting Alfoz to punch you was an interesting move. Agent Viira sure enjoyed it.
Smart move talking things out with the dwarves. Let's hope you can keep things civil moving forward as well.
As for those youngsters, brave of you to rush in like that. Lots of radicals on the streets these days.
Modissa and Rollo seem like they've been at war for quite some time. Maybe this won't be the last you see of them.
Then there's poor, poor Drummer. Trying to ship himself off into the unknown.
Hopefully he'll fare better in some far-off city. Good move sending him away.
Smart of you to keep him around. You'll probably get a chance to talk with him again before the election.
There's also the Hag. Someone holding a meeting in the tea shop? Right before the explosion? Highly suspicious.
There's also the Hag. Lisa is suspicious, but beyond her natural hag-ness, nothing seems to point in her direction.
By solving Olzis' riddle, you've clearly distinguished yourself. Just be careful what you do with your Deck...
By solving Olzis' riddle, you've clearly distinguished yourself. Though I'm genuinely surprised you didn't end the campaign outright by drawing from the Deck. Really. You're insane.
And sorry about letting you stumble into the City Below. I'm just surprised you made it out alive.
You really handled that fire-trap quite well. Couldn't have done it without Snell, eh?
Good to keep him at a distance though. You're not the type to make friends, anyhow.
The roper fight I did not anticipate. Especially that outcome. As in, that you didn't get eaten.
Though considering you waltzed right into that gelatinous cube... let's just say, you're real lucky to be alive.
And remember that you've got an entire dungeon underneath the city to explore as well...
But now it's time to deal with the main quest: The tea shop awaits.
But now for the far more mysterious question: Who killed the elf? And more importantly... why?
(And please, go to the goblin garden. It's to the south. They're waiting.)
You lay down on your bedroll, finding sleep difficult.
As you stir, you think about your quest. The Star Witness, the man-in-yellow.
Frank, son of Frank. It might just be a dead end- though you've got a distinct feeling that he's lurking somewhere below.
To think you've already discovered Meriadoc, saving him from that horrid troll. Figured it'd take you much longer.
But... you still haven't even entered the tea shop? It's probably time to do that tomorrow. Unless you want to be contrarian.
Which is fine. You're allowed to be contrarian. I'm just saying.
It's the 'mystery of the tea shop' campaign. Not the 'I'm gonna dungeon crawl all day' campaign.
Your star witness, Meriadoc Moonwatch, told you about his sighting of this... invisible smoking man.
Someone who has managed to enter the Pillar of Jor.
You know you must follow. Just make sure you're fully prepared...
As your mind wanders, you realize you still have not entered the tea shop. Your main quest here on Tolstad.
You've focused on a lot of other things, so it's understandable. But perhaps now it's time.
As your mind wanders, you get an intense feeling that you've missed something in the tea shop.
Whatever it is, you'll need to figure it out before you report to Lady Sageleaf.
And poor, poor Drummer. Trying to ship himself off into the unknown.
Then... there's the question of the elf.
This was supposed to be a simple job. No casualties. No pressure. Just some angry goblins and a ruined tea shop.
Now it appears to be anything but.
You really worked your ass off for the revolution. Then you even managed to help out Viira against that ambassador.
You really worked your ass off for the revolution. Then you even managed to do exactly what Viira wanted, in that talk with the ambassador. She's lucky to have you.
You really worked your ass off for the revolution. Only to get Viira pissed off at you during your meeting with the ambassador. It'll be interesting to see how you end up, in this new Norvik.
A true Freestrider is what you are, working so hard for the revolution. You know well: a bright future awaits in this new Norvik.
Helping out the Azgalists? Getting Modissa to tone down the rhetoric? You're really performing miracles among the dwarves.
Helping out the Azgalists? Helping Modissa push her rhetoric across the party line? Keep going like this, and you'll end up a true dialectician.
The Resistance. Not anymore. Sending those boys away was the smartest thing you could do for them.
Don't worry. They'll thank you in the end.
Those papers will make history. You won't be a part of it, of course. But Rollo and his boys will change the city - for the better.
Or at the very least, Modissa will make some wonderful noise before the Freestriders stomp them out.
Those papers will make history. You won't be a part of it, of course. But those kids will change the city - for the better.
Or at the very least, they'll make some wonderful noise before the Freestriders stomp them out.
Oh, and by solving Olzis' riddle, you've clearly distinguished yourself. Just be careful what you do with your Deck...
So many loose threads. But don't worry, you've got time.
You'll still need to locate the tea shop owner.
It's time to delve deeper, past the Below. Among its many secrets, some path has to go deeper...
Your delving has gone well, but it's time to look elsewhere. To shine a light on the other corners of Tolstad...
Before you know, eight hours have passed. You successfully complete your long rest.
As you fall into the softness of the bedroll, in this tiny tower...
You feel tired. The kind of tired sleep won't fix.
Three days. Three days you've spent on Tolstad, without even once poking your head down into the City Below.
Might be time. The mystery of the man-in-yellow clearly leads that way.
Then there's the Hag. Someone holding a meeting in the tea shop? Right before the explosion? Highly suspicious.
Then there's the Hag. Lisa is suspicious, but beyond her natural hag-ness, nothing seems to point in her direction.
Finally, your star witness: Meriadoc Moonwatch. He told you about his sighting of this... invisible smoking man.
You know you must follow. It's time to finish the job.
Will you be able to complete this quest of yours?
Below the Below. That is where you must go.
The Undercoast Path. Beyond that mushroom jungle.
That is where you will find your answers...
Answers within Strings.
You close your eyes to begin this desperate plea for sleep.
The Strings you follow, all are tangled around this endless Pillar spiked through the heart of the city.
Poor, poor Drummer. Trying to ship himself off into the unknown.
And by solving Olzis' riddle, you've clearly distinguished yourself. Just be careful what you do with your Deck...
And by solving Olzis' riddle, you've clearly distinguished yourself. Though I'm genuinely surprised you didn't end the campaign outright by drawing from the Deck. Really. You're insane.
You've explored every possibility. Followed each red thread.
Except one. The man-in-yellow. Your Frank son of Frank.
A whisper tells you: tomorrow, you WILL find him. In a corner of the City Below...
You realize it clearly, lying here. Past Hallway of Fire. That is the final place to look.
You realize it clearly, lying here. Past Hallway of Fire. There was a staircase guarded by the assassin. That is where you must go.
Finally, to enter the Pillar you must perform a most challenging esoteric task: Travel to the Beyond.
There are many esoteric beings on Tolstad. Some of whom are already known to you. One of them will surely assist you.
You've managed to hand that Scroll of Astral Projection to Visken. Quite the find. Now you must find the courage to ask him to use it.
You've managed to get that attuned emerald from Olzis. Quite the charmer you are, to get her to help you out. Or maybe she was just bored. Either way- now you're ready.
Selling your soul for the opportunity seems almost worth it. Despite his appearance, Ever-Glad doesn't seem that much worse of a patron than most employers in the city.
Is this your last night on Tolstad? Is this your last night alive?
As the sun rises over your beloved city, you know one thing true...
It is time to enter the Pillar.
The truth lies Below the Below.
This is it. The last day before the election.
You can barely sleep. Though it still counts as a long rest, lucky you.
As you wake, slowly, on this final day before the election, you know each moment will feel like a lifetime. As if all of Norvik is holding its breath.
Focus and prepare. Put everything in order. It's time.
Finish the campaign.
Another day.
Another adventure.
You successfully complete a long rest. Congratulations.
There's only one thing left to do.
Find the Star Witness. Unveil the truth...
Unveil the truth. Go into the Beyond...
The first day.
Your muscles strain as the second day begins.
Another day full of trouble.
The END is near.
Today you need to gather more evidence. This mystery will not solve itself.
You should have evidence to solve this. It's not that difficult.
It is time to open your heart. The people of Tolstad cry out for you.
You're unsure exactly what to do this forenoon. Perhaps a walk, to start things off?
You really gotta finish this today. Or else people are gonna talk.
If you want to finish this today, then it's time to put on the rough gloves.
Which means... yelling in people's faces? Or something like that.
Two days. Remaining.
It is actually only one day remaining.
You should be embarrassed to get it wrong like that.
Sic.
One day. Remaining.
(Start your day.)
This is literally how you feel, like, fifty percent of the time.
You should go to bed earlier.
Like a man.
More sleep would help.
Perhaps... tomorrow.
Going to bed early. Smart.
Acting like a real man.
A few extra hours of sleep...
Does <shake>wonders</shake>.
Because you are... and were...
Gotta keep running around if you want to get shit done.
Ignore those tired legs! Keep on running!
Do you?
You do not remember them.
Fragments. Whispers. A voice that isn't yours.
The stress of a new job. Get yourself together.
New city. New tower. New bedroll. New-ish.
You'll be a little scatter-brained. It is what it is.
Some say dreams are the mortal mind's way of receiving divinations.
But that's bullshit. Just don't think about it, okay?
Your Patriarch for one.
There are rumors that the Lawlord is putting a lot of pressure on your superiors.
Yes, Alemikan has been very thorough in his management of the Urthguard as of late. In preparation for this foolish election.
If you cause trouble - if you don't handle this - there will be trouble.
Even more so than last time.
Last time was bullshit. Everyone knows it.
You just didn't handle it with style. Next time will be different.
Somehow, you doubt that. Through simple pattern recognition.
Hells yeah, brother.
Time to get to work!
How are you ever gonna find the time...?
<wiggle>Stress</wiggle>...
Time moves fast when you're running around like a headless chicken.
Time moves fast when you're productive.
The election looms.
HOME.
A real man needs nothing more.
Than a bedroll and some old planks? In a hole-filled tower? That keeps swaying in the wind?
You miss your bed.
Home, with mom...
Dear mom.
Not like she'd be home.
Yeah. She's busy. Out hustling, like always. Like she should!
You must finish this.
You must try to focus. Despite all the horrors of this world.
Eh. Don't worry about it.
You have a feeling you're gonna finish this job just on time. As per usual.
THE FINAL DAY.
Everything ends today.
Or begins. Depending on your perspective.
Depending on which party wins this foolish democratic process.
